newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes retreat late, diffs flat.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes retreat late, diffs flat.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices retreated in late trade on Monday after they rallied with gasoline, while differentials stayed flat.
Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude shifted to a December West Texas Intermediate (WTI) basis without a single fixed deal off November, traders said.
The discount was $2.30 off December WTI.
Buyers were scarce last month because profit margins weakened early this quarter. This prompted Ultramar to push back maintenance on a California coker to this week.

A trader said Tosco would cut runs by 10,000 barrels-per-day from Tuesday. NYMEX Crude ended a penny lower, but gained as much as 49 cents a barrel before settling at $24.85 a barrel. Outright prices for ANS ended $22.30/22.70 a barrel Monday, with December WTI closing at $24.70/24.80 a barrel.

Ultramar Corp began unspecified run cuts at its Wilmington, Calif, refinery over the weekend. Cuts came after workers shut a coker and other units, an industry source said. Wilmington crude held at $18.90/19 a barrel. Kern River heavy crude also held, ranging $17.40.17.60 a barrel, with majors and a large independent refiner rumored to offer cargoes.
